contradictions: NLM's closed per-block Block containers and new render/container.rs plus theme/ansi16.rs would add a second physical container layer; the repository already has live_surface_block, AlertEdge, semantic rails, and bounded live projection.
The 16ms, O(k/n), exact narrow-width policy, and breathing border claims are not local acceptance facts; citations and sources_used are empty.

A full rectangular border can consume cells and rows, collide with Markdown/CJK wrapping, and duplicate the existing live-surface border; only a same-row boundary cue is compatible until a stronger local defect is demonstrated.

unverified_hypotheses.hypothesis: At a visible transition from one anchored semantic block to another, the existing rail marks the new block but leaves the preceding block visually open; a same-row bottom glyph at that transition can close the cue without adding physical rows.
support: CodeGraph shows live_rail derives only previous LiveLineKind and AlertEdge handles Markdown alerts, not LiveBlockFocus transitions.
against: Visible rows are deliberately assembled into bounded Answer/Reasoning/Tool lanes, so a transition is a presentation boundary rather than an execution chronology.
unverified_hypotheses.experiment: Derive a bounded block-end flag from adjacent visible LiveLineAnchor focuses, replace only the preceding semantic rail at transitions, and test CJK/Markdown/resize plus unchanged row count.

candidates.core: Add a same-row semantic block-end cue to the existing live rail: when adjacent visible anchored rows change LiveBlockFocus, the preceding rail becomes a colored bottom marker; no new Block, row, parser, or layout layer is introduced.
constraints: reuse LiveLineAnchor, live_rail, existing ANSI16 roles and bounded projection
do not override Markdown AlertEdge or fenced-code rails
preserve tool folding, focus contrast, Follow/HOLD, keys, queue, execution/provider/MCP and cache semantics
risks: lane ordering is presentation-owned and must not be described as execution chronology
last visible tail row has no inferred closure when the next block is clipped; avoid guessing
validation: Reasoning→Answer and Tool→Answer boundary regressions with unchanged physical row count

recommendation: Reject full per-block rectangular containers as local overlap and layout risk. Accept only a transition-boundary rail cue if the local regression proves the previous block is visually open and the cue preserves cell width and physical rows.

next_step.value: Implement and verify the bounded adjacent-anchor block-end rail cue in the existing renderer.

stop_conditions: Do not add a second renderer, physical container rows, global sidebar, virtualizer, fixed frame threshold, or execution state.
Do not remap Tab/Enter or query excluded user-owned deep-research status.
Do not delete the sole Active Note.
